# `build/` — Pipeline definitions

This directory contains Azure DevOps pipeline YAML files and the pod-scheduler
configs that generate them.

## Generated files (do not edit by hand)

The CI pipelines that run the daily benchmark sweep are generated by the
[pod-scheduler](../scripts/pod-scheduler/README.md). Each pipeline maps to a
JSON config that lists the available pods (machine groups) and scenarios.

| Generated YAML | Source config | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `benchmarks-ci-01.yml`, `benchmarks-ci-02.yml` | `benchmarks_ci_pods.json` | On-prem fleet (Gold); split across two YAMLs to spread load |
| `benchmarks-ci-azure.yml` | `benchmarks_ci_azure_pods.json` | Azure cloud pods (includes the merged eastus2 cobalt cloud pods) |
| `benchmarks-ci-cobalt.yml` | `benchmarks_ci_cobalt_pods.json` | Cobalt-hosted pods |

To regenerate, from the repo root:

```bash
python ./scripts/pod-scheduler/main.py \
    --config ./build/benchmarks_ci_pods.json \
    --yaml-output ./build

python ./scripts/pod-scheduler/main.py \
    --config ./build/benchmarks_ci_azure_pods.json \
    --base-name benchmarks-ci-azure \
    --yaml-output ./build

python ./scripts/pod-scheduler/main.py \
    --config ./build/benchmarks_ci_cobalt_pods.json \
    --base-name benchmarks-ci-cobalt \
    --yaml-output ./build
```

The header of each generated YAML embeds the exact regen command for that
file.

The `citrine1`, `citrine2`, and `citrine3` names in the on-prem config are
controller queues, not retired benchmark machines or relay targets.

## Hand-maintained scenario templates

Everything else in this directory is hand-maintained. The most important
groups:

- `*-scenarios.yml` — AzDO job templates that the generated pipelines invoke
  (e.g. `proxies-scenarios.yml`, `grpc-scenarios.yml`). One per benchmark
  family. The pod-scheduler picks which template to run via the
  `template` field on each scenario in the JSON config.
- `prbenchmarks.yml` — scheduled PR-benchmark bot pipeline.
- `prbenchmarks.*.config.yml` — components, scenarios, and machine choices for
  individual PR-benchmark requests.
- `job-variables.yml` — shared variable definitions consumed by the scenario
  templates.

When adding a new benchmark family, drop a `*-scenarios.yml` template in this
directory and reference it from the relevant `benchmarks_ci_*_pods.json`.

## PR benchmarks

`prbenchmarks.yml` polls benchmark requests on `dotnet/aspnetcore`,
`dotnet/efcore`, and `dotnet/runtime` every 30 minutes. The controller image
determines where PR components are built, not which machine runs the benchmark.
The first profile in each bot config is the default machine selection.

| Config | Controller | Supported benchmark machines (default first) |
|---|---|---|
| `prbenchmarks.aspnetcore.config.yml` | Windows | `aspnet-gold-lin`, `aspnet-gold-win` (x64, 56 cores) |
| `prbenchmarks.efcore.config.yml` | Windows | `aspnet-gold-win` (x64, 56 cores) |
| `prbenchmarks.runtime.windows_x64.config.yml` | Windows | `aspnet-gold-win` (x64, 56 cores) |
| `prbenchmarks.runtime.linux_x64.config.yml` | Linux | `aspnet-gold-lin` (x64, 56 cores) |

These selections use the existing `aspnet-gold-*-relay` profiles imported by
the benchmark scenarios. Gold Linux uses `goldlin`, `goldload`, and `golddb`;
Gold Windows uses `goldwin`, `goldload2`, and `golddb`. The disconnected Perf
and Citrine choices are no longer offered. Runtime ARM64 jobs/configs have
been retired because their relay machines are unavailable; Gold is x64 and
does not replace ARM64 coverage.

The ASP.NET Core, EF Core, and runtime scenario/component definitions are
unchanged. This migration does not change the polling schedule, controller
images, or Crank SDK/build configuration.

## Editing the schedule

Common edits, all done in JSON:

- **Add a scenario**: append to `scenarios[]` in the appropriate
  `benchmarks_ci_*_pods.json`.
- **Add a pod / machine class**: append to `pods[]` and reference its name
  from any scenario you want to target it.
- **Change cadence or splits**: edit `metadata.schedule` (cron),
  `metadata.yaml_generation.target_yaml_count`, or
  `metadata.yaml_generation.schedule_offset_hours`.
- **Override a job's timeout**: add `"timeout": <minutes>` to the scenario.

After any edit, regenerate the YAML and commit both the JSON and the YAML
together. The snapshot tests in
`scripts/pod-scheduler/tests/test_snapshots.py` will fail in CI if the
generated YAML drifts from the configs.

## Build reuse within a pipeline run

`build-reuse.profile.yml` supplies opt-in Crank profiles for the high-repeat
container, gRPC, HttpClient, SignalR, and WebSocket matrices. Their scenario
templates load `$(buildReuseProfile)` and pass
`--variable buildCacheId=$(Build.BuildId)`. The first use of each build on an
agent checks out sources and builds; later compatible entries reuse it. A new
pipeline build ID changes both the source key and the build key, so floating
branches, .NET versions, and Docker base images are refreshed on the next run.
`--session` alone does not invalidate Crank caches. Source and build keys have
different prefixes because their metadata lives in the same cache directory.

| Suite | Builds reused across entries |
|---|---|
| Containers | Application and database images across 9 sizes and 3 request rates |
| gRPC | Separate ASP.NET Core/Go servers and .NET/Go/h2load clients across calls, protocols, and connection/stream counts |
| HttpClient | Client and Kestrel server across GET/POST, HTTP versions, concurrency, and payload sizes |
| SignalR | Server and client across scenarios, transports, and protocols; warmup and load share the client build |
| WebSockets | Client across payload sizes; separate compressed/uncompressed server builds |

These profiles reuse builds, not running processes or database contents.
Containers and applications are still started and stopped for each benchmark;
warmup and measurement durations are unchanged. Caches are local to each agent,
not shared between machines or architectures, and remain subject to the agent's
normal cache cleanup/lifetime. These profiles do not add a cache TTL; retained
builds need the same agent cleanup/restart policy as other Crank caches.

Container cache keys include the image name. Different Dockerfiles must have
different image names; the ASP.NET default, Alpine, Composite, and current
variants therefore have separate tags. gRPC scenario entries specify
`serverBuildKey` and `clientBuildKey` to separate implementations, and WebSocket
server keys include the compile-time compression mode. When adding a new
compile-time variant to these matrices, give it a distinct build identity
rather than reusing an existing key.

Other potential follow-ups are the proxy payload/protocol matrix and the
baseline/trend suites. They are not opted in here: proxies vary configuration
files copied into Docker images, while baseline/trend suites vary projects,
frameworks, and publishing settings that need their own cache identities.
The SslStream/QUIC matrix is currently disabled. Build-performance benchmarks
must continue building because build time is what they measure.

To check cache isolation without contacting agents or running benchmarks:

```bash
python -m unittest discover -s build/tests
```

The profile tests use the existing `crank --debug` configuration-only mode and
skip when the Crank CLI is not installed. Template wiring checks run without it.

## Minimal Todo

`minimal-todo-scenarios.yml` dispatches `scenarios/minimal-todo/minimal-todo.benchmarks.yml`
(1 CPU, 536,870,912 bytes / 512 MiB, 25200 req/s, enabled) for the `gold-lin`
and Azure `azure-arm64`/`cobalt-cloud-lin` pods. C# runs on every regular
scheduled slot using the direct (non-Docker) `csharp-project` build; Go and
Rust run the Docker `go`/`rust` builds but only on a shared weekly slot
(`condition: Math.round(Date.now() / 43200000) % 14 == 0`, combined with the
pod's own condition, matching the `containers-scenarios.yml` idiom). The
Docker `csharp`/`go`/`rust` builds (floating, multi-arch base images, no
pinned digests, no `requiredArchitecture` gating) remain the canonical
generation/update/admission/pre-promotion comparison path and are unaffected
-- see `scenarios/minimal-todo/README.md` for the full execution-path
mapping. Generation, admission, and calibration tooling for this cohort live
in the separate `dotnet-performance-tools`
repository; this directory only carries the scheduled dispatch template.
